literal: After elder brother Shen's rebellion, he resigned from office for a short time.
idiomatic: After his elder brother Shen rebelled, he resigned from office for a time.

literal: Sima Xiaonan, Yellow Gate Attendant, was the son of Left Vice Director Ziru and also a son-in-law of Gao Zu; his power was great at the time.
idiomatic: Sima Xiaonan of the Yellow Gate was the son of Left Vice Director Sima Ziru and a son-in-law of Gao Huan — a man whose power stood at its height.

literal: On an off-hour after leaving court, he sought out Jishi and drank deeply with him.
idiomatic: One day after court, in the idle hours of his leave, he sought out Gao Jishi and drank with him until they were both well beyond sober.

literal: He stayed overnight until dawn; both inner and outer gates were shut and bolted.
idiomatic: Xiaonan stayed the night through until dawn; every gate, inner and outer, was shut and barred.

literal: Xiaonan earnestly pleaded: "I am a Yellow Gate Attendant, a minister attending upon the Son of Heaven — how could there be any question of my not attending court?
idiomatic: Xiaonan pleaded earnestly: "I am a Yellow Gate Attendant, a minister who attends the Son of Heaven — how can I fail to appear at court?

literal: And I have already been away one night; my father will surely be greatly alarmed.
idiomatic: I have already been gone one night; my father will surely be alarmed beyond measure.

literal: If you keep me here drinking wildly again, I will have no defense against charges, and I fear you too will not escape censure."
idiomatic: If you keep me here for another night of wild drinking, I will have no defense when I am charged — and I fear you will not escape censure either."

literal: Jishi said: "You call yourself a Yellow Gate Attendant, and say you fear your father's alarm — do you mean to intimidate me with your family position?
idiomatic: Jishi said: "You call yourself a Yellow Gate Attendant and speak of fearing your father's wrath — do you mean to intimidate me with your family's standing?

literal: Gao Jishi's death will come where it should; I truly fear nothing of this."
idiomatic: Gao Jishi will die where and when he must; I fear nothing of this."

literal: Xiaonan bowed in apology and asked to leave, but was never permitted.
idiomatic: Xiaonan bowed and begged to be released, but permission never came.

literal: When wine was brought, he refused to drink.
idiomatic: When wine was brought, he would not drink.

literal: Jishi said: "I keep you here to drink your fill — what manner of man are you, that you won't drink deeply for me?"
idiomatic: Jishi said: "I keep you here to drink your fill — what sort of guest are you, that you will not drink deeply for me?"

literal: He ordered attendants to fetch cart-wheel rims to clamp around Xiaonan's neck, and fetched another rim to clamp around his own neck; then he ordered wine and, cups filled to the brim, urged each other to drink.
idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to fetch cart-wheel rims and clamp one around Xiaonan's neck; he fetched another and clamped it around his own. Then he ordered wine, filled the cups to the brim, and urged each other to drink.

literal: Xiaonan had no choice; he laughed and complied, and only then did they both remove the cart wheels — and he was kept another night.
idiomatic: Xiaonan had no choice; he laughed and drank. Only then did they remove the wheels — and he was kept another night.

literal: At that time Xiaonan had been missing two nights; no one knew where he was, and within and without all were astonished.
idiomatic: Xiaonan had now been missing two nights; no one knew where he was, and court and city alike were astonished.

literal: When Xiaonan emerged, he told the full story.
idiomatic: When Xiaonan at last emerged, he told the whole story.

literal: Shizong was administering affairs in the capital; he reported to the Wei emperor and had fine wine in several shi and delicacies in ten carts bestowed on Xiaonan, and had court gentlemen who were close with Jishi gather for a banquet at Jishi's residence.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng was administering affairs in the capital; he reported to the Wei emperor and had several shi of fine wine and ten cartloads of delicacies bestowed on Xiaonan, and ordered court gentlemen who were close to Jishi to gather for a banquet at Jishi's residence.

literal: Such was the favor shown him.
idiomatic: Such was the favor he received.

literal: Yi's eldest brother's son Yongle and second brother's son Yanbo were both called gentle and generous, men of elder bearing; both followed Yi in raising the banner of revolt.
idiomatic: Gao Yi's eldest brother's son Yongle and his second brother's son Yanbo were both called gentle and generous, men of elder bearing; both followed Yi when he raised the banner of revolt.

literal: Yongle reached the offices of guard general, right grand master of splendid happiness, and chief elder of Ji Province; he went out as governor of Boling but, unable to manage the people's affairs, killed himself.
idiomatic: Yongle rose to guard general, right grand master of splendid happiness, and chief elder of Ji Province; he went out as governor of Boling, but unable to manage the people's affairs, he took his own life.

literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, supervisor of military affairs in Cang and Ji provinces, third-grade equal to imperator, and governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, supervisor of military affairs in Cang and Ji provinces, third-grade equal to imperator, and governor of Ji Province.

literal: His son Changming was born of a lowly concubine and was not formally acknowledged until he was over twenty.
idiomatic: His son Changming was born of a lowly concubine and was not formally acknowledged until he was past twenty.

literal: Fierce and cruel, he loved killing, yet he was also resolute in battle.
idiomatic: Fierce and cruel, he loved killing — yet in battle he was resolute.

literal: At first he held the Great Xia Gate against Erzhu Shilong and, for merit accumulated, was promoted to left grand master of splendid happiness.
idiomatic: At first he held the Great Xia Gate against Erzhu Shilong and, for accumulated merit, rose to left grand master of splendid happiness.

literal: Gao Zu remotely appointed Changming governor of Yong Province and enfeoffed him as baron of Juyang township, one hundred households.
idiomatic: Gao Huan remotely appointed Changming governor of Yong Province and enfeoffed him baron of Juyang township with a fief of one hundred households.

literal: Soon he was further enfeoffed as count of Yanling county, with two hundred households added; during Wuding, he followed Equal-to-Imperator Liu Feng in campaigning against Hou Jing and was killed by Jing.
idiomatic: Soon he was further enfeoffed count of Yanling county, with two hundred households added; during Wuding he followed equal-to-imperator Liu Feng against Hou Jing and was killed by Jing.

literal: Posthumously granted governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted governor of Ji Province.

literal: Yanbo served through gentleman of the palace interior and governor of An Province, enfeoffed baron of Wannian county with a fief of two hundred households.
idiomatic: Yanbo served as gentleman of the palace interior and governor of An Province, and was enfeoffed baron of Wannian county with a fief of two hundred households.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was additionally made general who campaigns west and advanced in rank to viscount.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was additionally made general who campaigns west and advanced in rank to viscount.

literal: He died; posthumously granted vice director of the imperial treasury.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously he was granted vice director of the imperial treasury.

literal: From the time Ang first made a name as a bold swordsman, those who served as his wings were: Huyan Zu, Liu Guizhen, Liu Changdi, Dongfang Lao, Liu Shirong, Cheng Wubiao, Han Yuansheng, Liu Taobang;
idiomatic: From the time Gao Ang first made a name as a bold swordsman, those who served as his wings were Huyan Zu, Liu Guizhen, Liu Changdi, Dongfang Lao, Liu Shirong, Cheng Wubiao, Han Yuansheng, and Liu Taobang;

literal: Those who followed him in raising the standard were: Li Xiguang, Liu Shuzong, Liu Menghe.
idiomatic: those who followed him in raising the standard were Li Xiguang, Liu Shuzong, and Liu Menghe.

literal: All rose to distinction in official service.
idiomatic: All rose to distinction in official service.

literal: Shuzong, styled Yuanzuan, was a man of Pingchang in Leling.
idiomatic: Liu Shuzong, styled Yuanzuan, was a man of Pingchang in Leling.

literal: Harmonious and cautious, he possessed considerable learning and passed the provincial examination.
idiomatic: Harmonious and cautious, he possessed considerable learning and passed the provincial examination.

literal: He was gradually promoted to administrative aide of Cang Province.
idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to administrative aide of Cang Province.

literal: During the Yong'an era he was additionally made general who pacifies the distant and remonstrance advisor.
idiomatic: During the Yong'an era he was additionally made general who pacifies the distant and remonstrance advisor.

literal: His elder brother Haibao, from youth lightly chivalric, was nonetheless beloved by the district.
idiomatic: His elder brother Haibao, from youth lightly chivalric, was nonetheless beloved throughout the district.

literal: When Ang raised the banner of revolt, Haibao led the village folk in a raid on Cang Province to respond to Ang; Ang put Haibao in provisional charge of Cang Province affairs.
idiomatic: When Ang raised the banner of revolt, Haibao led the village folk in a raid on Cang Province to answer him; Ang put Haibao in provisional charge of Cang Province affairs.

literal: Former Fan Yang governor Diao Zheng, whose heart sided with Erzhu, dispatched his nephew's son Anshou to raid and kill Haibao.
idiomatic: Former Fan Yang governor Diao Zheng, whose heart sided with the Erzhu, dispatched his nephew's son Anshou to raid and kill Haibao.

literal: Shuzong thereupon returned to Ang.
idiomatic: Shuzong thereupon returned to Ang.

literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing, Gao Zu appointed him former general and vice director of the court of justice.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing, Gao Huan appointed him former general and vice director of the court of justice.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was additionally made general who pacifies the army and grand master of splendid happiness.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was additionally made general who pacifies the army and grand master of splendid happiness.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was made general of chariots and cavalry and left grand master of splendid happiness.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was made general of chariots and cavalry and left grand master of splendid happiness.

literal: He died in the second year.
idiomatic: He died in the second year.

literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, equal to imperator, and governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, equal to imperator, and governor of Ding Province.

literal: Lao was a man of Ande in Ge.
idiomatic: Dongfang Lao was a man of Ande in Ge.

literal: His family had been humble for generations.
idiomatic: His family had been humble for generations.

literal: He stood seven feet tall and his physical strength surpassed other men.
idiomatic: He stood seven feet tall, and his physical strength surpassed other men.

literal: In youth he was rough and lawless; he joined light and reckless men in forming a band of robbers, and the district suffered from them.
idiomatic: In youth he was rough and lawless; he joined light and reckless men in forming a band of robbers, and the district suffered for it.

literal: When warfare arose at the end of Wei, he joined Ang's retinue.
idiomatic: When warfare arose at the end of Wei, he joined Ang's retinue.

literal: When the banner of righteousness was raised, he still followed on campaign and, for military merit, was appointed general of the palace interior.
idiomatic: When the banner of righteousness was raised, he followed on campaign and, for military merit, was appointed general of the palace interior.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to general who pacifies the distant.
idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to general who pacifies the distant.

literal: He was appointed governor of Luoyang.
idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Luoyang.

literal: Later he was made governor of Southern Yi Province, concurrently governor of Yiyang, and granted the title of Viscount of Changle.
idiomatic: Later he was made governor of Southern Yi Province, concurrently governor of Yiyang, and granted the title of viscount of Changle.

literal: Lao governed two provinces in succession, entering and leaving over several years; his territory bordered many barbarian tribes and also neighbored the western enemy. In storming cities and field battles he always led the van of the troops; repeatedly he used the few to overcome the many, and the western enemies feared him.
idiomatic: Lao governed two provinces in succession over several years; his territory bordered many barbarian tribes and neighbored the western enemy. In storming cities and field battles he always led from the van; repeatedly he used the few to overcome the many, and the western enemies feared him.

literal: When Emperor Xianzu received the abdication, he was separately enfeoffed count of Yangping county and transferred to governor of Southern Yan Province.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang received the abdication, Lao was separately enfeoffed count of Yangping county and transferred to governor of Southern Yan Province.

literal: Later he crossed the Yangtze with Xiao Gui and others and died in battle.
idiomatic: Later he crossed the Yangtze with Xiao Gui and others and died in battle.

literal: Xiguang was a man of Gaocheng in Bohai.
idiomatic: Li Xiguang was a man of Gaocheng in Bohai.

literal: His father Shao was governor of Changguang in Wei; Xiguang followed Gao Gan in raising the revolt at Xindu.
idiomatic: His father Shao was governor of Changguang in Wei; Xiguang followed Gao Gan in raising the revolt at Xindu.

literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was appointed general who pacifies the south and governor of Ande commandery.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was appointed general who pacifies the south and governor of Ande commandery.

literal: Later he served as chief administrator of the heir apparent's office.
idiomatic: Later he served as chief administrator of the heir apparent's office.

literal: At the end of Wuding he followed Gao Yue in pacifying Yingchuan, was enfeoffed marquis of Yining county with an open fief, and served as governor of Ying, Liang, and Southern Yan provinces in succession.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he followed Gao Yue in pacifying Yingchuan, was enfeoffed marquis of Yining county with an open fief, and served in succession as governor of Ying, Liang, and Southern Yan provinces.

literal: During Tianbao he was governor of Yang Province; crossing the Yangtze with Xiao Gui and others, he died in battle.
idiomatic: During Tianbao he was governor of Yang Province; crossing the Yangtze with Xiao Gui and others, he died in battle.

literal: Posthumously granted opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators and governor of Western Yan Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators and governor of Western Yan Province.

literal: His son Ziling was outer-troops bureau attendant of the masters of writing.
idiomatic: His son Ziling was outer-troops bureau attendant of the masters of writing.

literal: At the end of Wuping he was unaffiliated palace attendant.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was unaffiliated palace attendant.

literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died while governor of Yi Province.
idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died while governor of Yi Province.

literal: Xiguang's clansman Zigong, for merit in the righteous banner, reached the rank of department director of the civil service bureau; later he became governor of Yan Province.
idiomatic: Xiguang's clansman Zigong, for merit in raising the righteous banner, reached the rank of department director of the civil service bureau; later he became governor of Yan Province.

literal: For greed and cruelty he was killed by Shizong.
idiomatic: For greed and cruelty he was killed by Gao Cheng.

literal: Emperor Xianzu, rebuking Chen for deposing Xiao Ming, ordered Equal-to-Imperator Xiao Gui to lead Xiguang, Dongfang Lao, Pei Yingqi, and Wang Jingbao with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to campaign against him.
idiomatic: Gao Yang, rebuking Chen for deposing Xiao Ming, ordered equal-to-imperator Xiao Gui to lead Xiguang, Dongfang Lao, Pei Yingqi, and Wang Jingbao with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry against him.

literal: In the third month of the seventh year they crossed the Yangtze and stormed and took Stone City.
idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year they crossed the Yangtze and stormed and took Stone City.

literal: The five commanders were equal in rank and status; Yingqi as palace attendant served as army overseer, Xiao Gui and Xiguang both served as grand generals — in the army they were mutually resistant in protocol and would not submit to one another; each pressed his own stratagems, and whenever they acted, they inevitably clashed.
idiomatic: The five commanders were equal in rank; Yingqi as palace attendant served as army overseer, while Xiao Gui and Xiguang both served as grand generals. In camp they resisted one another in protocol and would not submit; each pressed his own stratagems, and whenever they moved, they inevitably clashed.

literal: The army encamped below Danyang city; there came more than fifty days of steady rain, and when battle came their weapons were all unusable — hence the defeat and destruction.
idiomatic: The army encamped below Danyang city; more than fifty days of steady rain followed, and when battle came their weapons were all unusable — hence the defeat and destruction.

literal: The generals all died; of the soldiers, only twelve or thirteen percent returned — the equipment, grain, and supplies lost could not be counted.
idiomatic: The generals all died; of the soldiers, only twelve or thirteen percent returned — the equipment, grain, and supplies lost were beyond counting.

literal: The biographies of Xiao Gui and Wang Bao are omitted from the histories.
idiomatic: The biographies of Xiao Gui and Wang Bao are omitted from the histories.

literal: Pei Yingqi was a man of Hedong.
idiomatic: Pei Yingqi was a man of Hedong.

literal: His ancestors crossed the Huai in the Jin at its end and settled in Shouyang county in Huainan.
idiomatic: His ancestors crossed the Huai at the end of Jin and settled in Shouyang county in Huainan.

literal: His grandfather Yanxian followed Xue Andu into Wei and reached the office of governor of Zhao commandery.
idiomatic: His grandfather Yanxian followed Xue Andu into Wei and reached the office of governor of Zhao commandery.

literal: His father Yue was chancellor of Bohai.
idiomatic: His father Yue was chancellor of Bohai.

literal: Yingqi was clever and witty, fond of playful talk, unconstrained in ritual observance; he served Wei and reached chief administrator of Ding Province.
idiomatic: Yingqi was clever and witty, fond of playful talk, unconstrained in ritual observance; he served Wei and rose to chief administrator of Ding Province.

literal: Shizong brought him in as left aide of the mobile headquarters.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng brought him in as left aide of the mobile headquarters.

literal: During Tianbao he was director of judicial affairs and concurrent palace attendant; when he died in battle he was posthumously granted opener of a government office and left vice director of the masters of writing.
idiomatic: During Tianbao he was director of judicial affairs and concurrent palace attendant; when he died in battle he was posthumously granted opener of a government office and left vice director of the masters of writing.

literal: Feng Longzhi, styled Zuyi, pet name Pi, was a man of Gaocheng in Bohai.
idiomatic: Feng Longzhi, styled Zuyi, pet name Pi, was a man of Gaocheng in Bohai.

literal: His father Hui was minister of works of Wei.
idiomatic: His father Hui was minister of works of Wei.

literal: Longzhi's nature was generous and mild, with breadth of spirit.
idiomatic: Longzhi's nature was generous and mild, with breadth of spirit.

literal: In his weak-crown years he served as chief clerk of the province and commandery; he began office as gentleman attendant at court and served as head of the straight guard.
idiomatic: In his weak-crown years he served as chief clerk of the province and commandery; he began office as gentleman attendant at court and served as head of the straight guard.

literal: Prince of Runan Yue opened his government office; Longzhi served as middle army adjutant.
idiomatic: When Prince of Runan Yue opened his government office, Longzhi served as middle army adjutant.

literal: At first, during the Yan Chang era, the Daoist monk Faqing raised disorder in the Ji region and styled himself "Great Vehicle"; his followers numbered more than fifty thousand.
idiomatic: At first, during the Yan Chang era, the Daoist monk Faqing raised disorder in the Ji region and styled himself "Great Vehicle"; his followers numbered more than fifty thousand.

literal: Grand Commander Yuan Yao and Longzhi captured Faqing; he was granted the title of viscount of Wucheng.
idiomatic: Grand Commander Yuan Yao and Longzhi captured Faqing; Longzhi was granted the title of viscount of Wucheng.

literal: Soon he concurrently served as chief clerk of the secretariat and aide of the Henan intendant.
idiomatic: Soon he concurrently served as chief clerk of the secretariat and aide of the Henan intendant.

literal: At that time the gentry and commoners of Qing and Qi provinces rebelled; Longzhi was sent on a mission to comfort and instruct them, and they all immediately submitted.
idiomatic: At that time the gentry and commoners of Qing and Qi provinces rebelled; Longzhi was sent on a mission to comfort and instruct them, and they all immediately submitted.

literal: During Yong'an he served as chief administrator of the pacification army headquarters.
idiomatic: During Yong'an he served as chief administrator of the pacification army headquarters.

literal: Erzhu Zhao and others garrisoned Jinyang; the Wei court, because Hennei was a strategic chokepoint, appointed Longzhi general of soaring dragon and governor of Hennei; soon he was additionally granted bearer of the staff, rear general, acting general who pacifies the north, and grand commander of the commandery.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao and others garrisoned Jinyang; the Wei court, because Hennei was a strategic chokepoint, appointed Longzhi general of soaring dragon and governor of Hennei; soon he was additionally granted bearer of the staff, rear general, acting general who pacifies the north, and grand commander of the commandery.

literal: Before he had reached the commandery, Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang and Emperor Zhuang died in confinement.
idiomatic: Before he had reached the commandery, Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang and Emperor Zhuang died in confinement.

literal: Longzhi, because his father had been murdered, always harbored thoughts of revenge; for this reason he took his staff and marched east, planning to raise the standard of revolt.
idiomatic: Longzhi, because his father had been murdered, always harbored thoughts of revenge; for this reason he took his staff and marched east, planning to raise the standard of revolt.

literal: At that time Gao Gan told Longzhi: "Erzhu was violent and rebellious; disaster befell the Supreme One. Brother and I alike received the late emperor's extraordinary favor — how can we fail to give our bodies for the sovereign and avenge this shame?
idiomatic: At that time Gao Gan told Longzhi: "Erzhu was violent and rebellious; disaster befell the Supreme One. Brother and I alike received the late emperor's extraordinary favor — how can we fail to give our bodies for the sovereign and avenge this shame?

literal: Longzhi replied: "The nation's shame and our family's grievance cut to the marrow; to move while the moment is ripe — now is truly the time."
idiomatic: Longzhi replied: "The nation's shame and our family's grievance cut to the marrow; to move while the moment is ripe — now is truly the time."

literal: Thereupon with Gan and the others he fixed the plan; by night they raided the provincial city and took it.
idiomatic: Thereupon with Gan and the others he fixed the plan; by night they raided the provincial city and took it.

literal: Gan and the others, because Longzhi had long been trusted by the hometown folk, pushed him forward as governor.
idiomatic: Gan and the others, because Longzhi had long been trusted by the hometown folk, pushed him forward as governor.
